simya.title: From alchemy to chemistry
simya.summary: Learn how alchemy, which did not measure, turned into chemistry, which measures and weighs.

cards.p: Alchemy (from Arabic al-kīmiyā) is the ancestor of chemistry. It also existed in China and India. Its Western branch passed from Alexandria to the Islamic world and from there to Europe. In alchemy, real experiments and magic went hand in hand.

once.soru: Alchemists tried to transform substances by heating and mixing them. Which science is this work the ancestor of today?

secenekler.neden: Curiosity about changing matter and lab experiments slowly turned into chemistry.
Astronomy grew out of watching the sky. Alchemy dealt with matter.
Alchemy studied how substances change, not living things.

cards.p: Alchemists searched for a legendary substance that would turn cheap metals like lead into gold. They called it the philosopher's stone. They tried for centuries, but never made a single gram of gold.

cards.p: The other dream was an elixir of life that would cure disease and extend life. It was never found, but the interest in preparing medicines helped pharmacy and medical chemistry grow.

once.soru: Alchemists searched for an elixir of life to cure disease. Which profession did this search help develop?

secenekler.neden: Mixing plants and minerals to prepare an elixir slowly fed into pharmacy and medical chemistry.
Architecture is about buildings. The search for an elixir led to preparing medicines.
The search for an elixir turned toward preparing medicines, not toward the sky.

cards.p: Alchemists developed tools such as the furnace, the mortar, the glass flask and the alembic. Jabir ibn Hayyan is credited with making nitric and sulfuric acid, and al-Razi with obtaining alcohol.

once.soru: Alchemists could not make gold. So what did they leave to us?

secenekler.neden: Tools like the furnace, mortar, glass flask and alembic, along with their experience in experiments, became the basis of the chemistry lab.
No alchemist ever made gold, because no such method exists.
They missed their goal, but their experiments and tools passed on to chemistry.

cards.p: Heating a liquid and cooling its vapor back into a liquid is called distillation. Substances separate because their boiling points differ. Alchemists developed this method, and today it is used to make perfume and fuel.

cards.p: In his 1661 book The Sceptical Chymist, Robert Boyle questioned the idea of "four elements". He argued that every claim should be tested by experiment. For Boyle, a substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances is an element.

cards.key: If a substance breaks down into simpler substances, it is not an element.

cards.p: In a closed container the total mass does not change. This is called conservation of mass, and Lavoisier showed it in the 1770s. Burning is a substance combining with oxygen. This ended the idea that a substance called phlogiston leaves things as they burn.

cards.key: In an open container the mass can change. You only see conservation when you weigh everything.

cards.h: How did chemistry become a science?
cards.p: Alchemists hid what they knew and rarely measured. In chemistry, a claim is tested by experiment, and the result is measured and shared. The cycle of observation, hypothesis, experiment and conclusion is the scientific method.

etk.soru: Put each feature where it belongs: alchemy or chemistry as a science?
ogeler: Others could not repeat and check the experiments. This was a flaw of alchemy.
Lavoisier's precise weighing is the basis of modern chemistry.

cards.p:
• Alchemy searched for ways to transform matter and for the elixir of life, but failed.
• It left behind distillation and lab equipment.
• For Boyle, an element is a substance that cannot be broken into simpler substances.
• Lavoisier showed that mass is conserved in a closed container and that burning is combining with oxygen.
• Experiment and measurement are what made chemistry a science.

quiz.q: Match each name or experiment with what it gave to chemistry.
quiz.e: Al-Razi is credited with obtaining alcohol. Boyle defined the element by experiment, Lavoisier showed mass is conserved in a closed container, and electrolysis proved that water is a compound.

quiz.q: Apply Boyle's definition: put each substance in the right group.
ogeler: Water: breaks into H₂ and O₂
Oxygen: does not break into anything simpler
Limestone: gives lime and CO₂ when heated
Gold: does not break down in any way
Table salt: gives sodium and chlorine by electrolysis
Sulfur: does not break into anything simpler
quiz.e: Water, limestone and salt break down into simpler substances, so they are compounds. Oxygen, gold and sulfur do not break down by any chemical means, so they are elements.

quiz.q: Put the steps of the scientific method in order.
quiz.e: First you observe something, then you form a hypothesis that explains it. The hypothesis is tested by experiment, and a conclusion is drawn.

quiz.q: Acetone boils at 56 °C and water at 100 °C. If you distill an acetone–water mixture, which collects in the receiving flask first?
quiz.e: Acetone has the lower boiling point, so it evaporates first, condenses in the cooler and drips into the flask. Distillation separates by boiling point difference.
y: Water boils at a higher temperature. The substance with the lower boiling point evaporates first.
Their boiling points differ, so one evaporates first.
Distillation is used exactly to separate liquids with different boiling points.

once.soru: A chemist measures how much of each substance a medicine contains. Which branch is this?

secenekler.neden: Analytical chemistry finds which substances are in a sample and in what amounts.
Polymer chemistry studies long-chain substances such as plastics.
Industrial chemistry deals with large-scale production. Measuring what a substance contains is the job of analytical chemistry.

cards.p: A chemical engineer designs processes in a plant, a metallurgical engineer works with metals, and a pharmacist prepares medicines and advises on doses. Medicine, food, paint and cosmetics all depend on chemistry.

once.soru: Who explains to a patient how and how much of a medicine to take?

secenekler.neden: A pharmacist prepares the medicine and explains its dose and use.
A chemical engineer designs production processes and does not give medicine to patients.
A metallurgical engineer works with metals and alloys.

once.soru: Which one goes into the batter to make a cake rise?

secenekler.neden: Baking soda (NaHCO₃) gives off CO₂ gas when heated. These bubbles make the cake rise.
Caustic soda (NaOH) is a strong base and burns skin. It never goes into food.
Blue vitriol (copper sulfate) is toxic and used in farming. It never goes into food.

cards.p: In the lab you wear goggles, a lab coat and gloves. Acid is always added to water. Chemicals are never smelled or tasted. You do not eat in the lab, you do not pour waste down the sink, and you do not use unlabeled bottles.

once.soru: Which element is in hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood?

secenekler.neden: The iron in hemoglobin binds oxygen. Iron deficiency causes anemia.
Lead is a heavy metal that builds up in the body and causes harm.
Mercury is toxic and has no job in the body.

cards.p:
• Chemistry has branches and is used in many careers.
• In a symbol the first letter is a capital and the second is lowercase. The subscript in a formula shows the number of atoms.
• Compounds also have common names.
• Know the hazard symbols and follow the lab rules.
• Some elements are essential for the body, while heavy metals are harmful.

quiz.q: Match each substance with the hazard symbol you should see on its bottle.
quiz.e: Kerosene catches fire easily. Potassium nitrate gives off oxygen and makes burning more intense. Cyanide kills even in tiny amounts. Concentrated sulfuric acid eats away skin and metal.

quiz.q: Put each element in the right group.
quiz.e: Calcium works in bones and teeth, iron in hemoglobin, and sodium and potassium in nerve signals. Mercury, lead and cadmium build up in the body and damage organs.

quiz.q: How many atoms in total are in one H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> molecule?
quiz.e: Subscripts show the number of atoms. 2 H + 1 S + 4 O = 7 atoms. The subscript of S is 1, so it is not written.

quiz.q: What is the right way to dilute an acid?
o: Add the acid slowly to water
Pour water quickly onto the acid
Pour both into the container at once
Heat the acid, then add water
quiz.e: Acid is added slowly to water. If water is poured onto acid, the heat released boils the water and can splash the acid.
y: The first drops of water poured onto acid boil from the heat released and splash the acid. That is why acid is added slowly to water.
Pouring both at once does not stop the heat from being released out of control. Acid should be added to water a little at a time.
Heating the acid makes it more dangerous. Heat is released during dilution, so acid is added slowly to cold water.

madde.title: Matter and its properties
madde.summary: Everything around you is matter. Learn the states, types and changes of matter.

cards.p: Anything that has mass and takes up space is called matter. Water, air, stone and you are all matter. Light, sound and heat are not matter. They carry energy or are energy themselves.

secenekler.neden: Light has no mass and takes up no space. Light only carries energy.
Air is a mixture of gases and has mass and volume. A blown-up balloon shows this.
Water vapor is water in the gas state, and it has mass and volume.

cards.p: In a solid, particles are packed tightly in order and vibrate in place. In a liquid, particles are close together but slide past each other. That is why a liquid takes the shape of its container. In a gas, particles are far apart and fast, and they fill the whole container.

cards.p: An element is made of only one kind of atom (Fe, O₂) and cannot be broken into simpler substances. A compound forms when different atoms bond in a fixed ratio (H₂O), and it can be broken down by chemical means. Elements and compounds are both pure substances.

cards.p: In a mixture the substances keep their properties. A mixture that is the same everywhere, like sugar water, is homogeneous. One whose parts you can tell apart, like sandy water, is heterogeneous. Mixtures are separated by filtering or distillation.

ogeler: It is a change of state. Both ice and water are H₂O.
Sugar molecules spread through the water but do not change. When the water evaporates, the sugar is left behind.
Iron turns into iron oxide with oxygen and moisture.
Substances in the cut apple react with oxygen in the air.

cards.key: A physical change is often easy to reverse. A chemical change usually is not.

cards.p: Mass, volume and inertia belong to all matter, and they are called common properties. Density, melting and boiling point, and solubility are characteristic properties. You identify an unknown substance by these properties.

once.soru: Two bottles have lost their labels, and both hold a colorless liquid. Which measurement tells you which one is water?

secenekler.neden: Pure water boils at 100 °C at 1 atm. Boiling point is a characteristic property that identifies a substance.
Every substance has mass, and it depends on the amount. So it does not identify the substance.
Volume depends on the amount. Different liquids can have the same volume.

cards.p: Mass per unit volume is called density, and it is calculated with d = m / V. At the same temperature and pressure, every pure substance has a fixed density that identifies it. A substance less dense than water floats on it.

yorum: This substance is less dense than water and floats.

once.soru: Ice floats on water. How does the density of ice compare with water's?

secenekler.neden: A substance less dense than water floats. Ice has a density of about 0.92 g/cm³, and water about 1 g/cm³.
If it were denser than water, it would sink.
If they were equal, it would stay suspended in the water.

cards.p:
• Matter is anything with mass and volume, and it has three states.
• An element does not break down, while a compound breaks into its elements by chemical means.
• Mixtures can be homogeneous or heterogeneous.
• In a physical change the identity stays the same. In a chemical change a new substance forms.
• Density, melting point and boiling point identify a substance.

quiz.q: Put each event in the right group.
quiz.e: In melting, sublimation, fogging (condensation) and dissolving, the substance stays the same. A burning candle gives CO₂ and water. In a cooking egg the proteins permanently lose their shape (denaturation) and link together. Tarnished silver forms silver sulfide.

quiz.q: Match each change of state with its name.
quiz.e: A solid melts when it turns into a liquid. A liquid freezes when it turns into a solid and evaporates when it turns into a gas. A solid turning straight into a gas is sublimation, and the reverse is deposition.

quiz.q: A substance has a mass of 54 g and a volume of 20 cm³. What is its density in g/cm³?
quiz.e: Density is mass per unit volume. d = m / V = 54 / 20 = 2.7 g/cm³. This is the density of aluminum.
H₂O forms from different atoms bonded in a fixed ratio, and electrolysis splits it into H₂ and O₂.
y: O₂ is a molecule with two atoms, but both atoms are oxygen. So it is a molecule of an element.
In salt water, salt and water mix without bonding to each other. It is a mixture whose ratio can vary.
Fe is made of one kind of atom and cannot be broken into simpler substances. So it is an element.
